steps.name: Fixed-dispersion DE test, treated vs control liver sample
caveats: No biological replication exists in this dataset (1 treated, 1 control) — never report edgeR's FDR from this run as if it reflected empirically estimated biological variability

Do not silently fall back to DESeq2's default DESeq() call or edgeR's estimateDisp/estimateCommonDisp on this design — both require replicates and will either error or silently produce a degenerate/undefined dispersion estimate
TMM normalization with only 2 libraries is still valid but sensitive to a few highly-expressed genes dominating the correction; sanity-check normalization factors are not extreme outliers
steps.question: Which genes differ in expression between the single treated liver sample and the single control liver sample, using edgeR's exactTest with a fixed common dispersion (since dispersion cannot be estimated from one sample per group) and a distribution-free CPM log2 fold-change as a cross-check?

grounding.reason: edgeR user-guide documented workaround for RNA-seq designs without biological replicates: supply exactTest() a fixed common dispersion (BCV) instead of estimating one from the data, using human-appropriate BCV (~0.4) rather than the ~0.1 typical of inbred model organisms; corroborated by McCarthy, Chen & Smyth 2012 (PMID 22287627) on edgeR's empirical-Bayes handling of limited-replicate dispersion and by the broader literature (e.g. Schurch et al. 2015, arXiv:1505.02017) establishing that very low replicate counts already produce unreliable DE calls, which motivates flagging n=1 results as exploratory.

acceptance_criteria: Loads counts.csv (12000 genes x 2 sample columns, raw integer salmon counts) and metadata.csv (2 samples x condition), and confirms samples map to exactly one 'treated' and one 'control' group
Filters out genes with negligible expression (e.g. near-zero counts in both samples) before testing, documenting the filter threshold and how many genes remain

Builds an edgeR DGEList, applies TMM normalization (calcNormFactors), and runs exactTest with an explicitly fixed dispersion (BCV) value rather than estimateDisp/estimateCommonDisp, because n=1 per group provides no within-group variance to estimate empirically

States the fixed BCV value used and its literature justification (human RNA-seq without replicates conventionally analyzed with BCV around 0.4, i.e. dispersion ~0.16, since human biological variability exceeds that of inbred organisms) directly in the output report
Independently computes a log2 fold-change of CPM-normalized treated vs control values for every retained gene as a distribution-free companion metric

Outputs a full per-gene table (gene symbol, treated CPM, control CPM, log2FC, edgeR PValue, edgeR FDR under the fixed dispersion) sorted by significance/effect size, and a clearly separated shortlist of genes meeting both |log2FC|>=1 and fixed-dispersion FDR<0.05

Explicitly states in the output that with n=1 per condition, the fixed-dispersion p-values/FDR are conditional on an assumed (not estimated) biological variability and must be treated as an exploratory screening/ranking rather than confirmatory differential expression inference; downstream biological claims from this gene list require independent replication

steps.name: Pathway-level interpretation of the treated vs control ranked gene list
caveats: Do not threshold the ranked list to only 'significant' genes before running pre-ranked GSEA-style enrichment — that discards the rank information the method needs and reintroduces the same underpowered-cutoff problem this step is meant to avoid
WikiPathways gene sets use HGNC symbols already matching this dataset's gene identifiers — do not attempt an unnecessary ID conversion
steps.question: Do the genes ranked by treated-vs-control log2 fold change concentrate in coherent human liver-relevant biological pathways, using pre-ranked enrichment against a human pathway gene-set collection?

grounding.reason: Standard pre-ranked pathway enrichment practice for a fold-change-ranked bulk RNA-seq gene list; no specific published rule was retrieved for this exact no-replicate scenario, so this step is included as interpretive context only, per the plan narrative's explicit caveat that it does not substitute for the core DE table.

acceptance_criteria: Uses the full ranked gene list (log2FC of CPM, treated vs control) produced in T1S1 as input, not just the significance-filtered shortlist, since per-gene significance calls in this design are only exploratory

Runs pre-ranked (fgsea-style) enrichment against an organism-matched (Homo sapiens) pathway gene-set collection resolved from the environment's reference data (e.g. a WikiPathways human GMT keyed on HGNC gene symbols, matching the gene symbols already used in counts.csv)

Reports normalized enrichment scores, p-values and FDR per pathway, and explicitly flags that the underlying gene-level ranking derives from an unreplicated (n=1 vs n=1) comparison, so pathway results are hypothesis-generating context for the T1S1 gene table, not independent confirmatory evidence

If the intended organism-matched pathway reference is not resolvable in the environment at run time, the step reports that enrichment could not be performed rather than substituting a mismatched-organism gene set

plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE (no replicates)
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context is bulk RNA-seq (salmon-derived raw integer gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 3 columns => 2 samples after removing the gene-symbol column) from human liver, with exactly one treated sample and one control sample and explicitly no biological replication. Standard replicate-based dispersion estimation (DESeq2's per-gene dispersion fitting, edgeR's tagwise/trended dispersion from estimateDisp) is mathematically impossible with n=1 per group: there is no within-group variance to estimate. The only tractable route within the installed toolchain is edgeR's exactTest with a fixed, user-supplied common dispersion (BCV) rather than one estimated from the data — a documented edgeR workaround for datasets that lack replication, using conservative literature-typical BCV values for human data (e.g., BCV=0.4, dispersion=0.16) since human biological variability is much higher than that of inbred model organisms. Because that dispersion is assumed rather than measured, resulting p-values/FDR are conditional on the assumption and must be reported as an exploratory/candidate ranking, not confirmatory statistical inference — this is stated explicitly as a caveat and complemented with a simple CPM-based log2 fold-change ranking that requires no distributional assumption at all, so genes flagged by both approaches are the more defensible candidates. Genes are already HGNC gene symbols, matching the organism-appropriate WikiPathways human gene-set collection available in the environment, so a lightweight fgsea pre-ranked enrichment on the full log2FC-ranked gene list (which avoids needing an arbitrary significance cutoff on underpowered per-gene tests) is added purely to help interpret the direction/coherence of the candidate gene signal — it does not substitute for the core deliverable, which is the per-gene treated-vs-control differential expression table with fold changes and both p-value/FDR (fixed-dispersion) and rank-based evidence.
